simple: the operating-system part that owns a GPU and lets programs use it safely.
analogy: the interpreter assigned to the visiting theatre company.
precise: kernel code that brings the GPU up (PCI, power, clocks), loads the firmware of its microcontrollers, manages GPU memory and GPU page tables, accepts and schedules command submissions, tracks their completion with fences, recovers from hangs, drives the display engine, and exposes all of this to user-space drivers through device files and ioctls. Not the same thing as a GPU kernel, the function a GPU runs (HW301).
source: D1 of F4-42 (Linux kernel community, Linux kernel documentation, "GPU Driver Developer's Guide" (Documentation/gpu/): "DRM Internals", "DRM Memory Management", "Kernel Mode Setting (KMS)", "GPU Scheduler", "Buffer Sharing and Synchronization", the amdgpu chapter (curriculum item 86)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D10 of F4-42 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 15.1 "What a GPU kernel driver does" and milestone G1 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build

simple: Linux's common framework for graphics drivers.
analogy: the school's standard booking rules that every visiting company's interpreter follows.
precise: the Linux kernel subsystem that GPU drivers plug into; it provides device nodes (a primary "card" node and "render" nodes), buffer-object management (GEM, TTM), a GPU scheduler, fences, and the kernel mode-setting (KMS) interface for displays.
source: D1 of F4-42 (Linux kernel community, Linux kernel documentation, "GPU Driver Developer's Guide" (Documentation/gpu/): "DRM Internals", "DRM Memory Management", "Kernel Mode Setting (KMS)", "GPU Scheduler", "Buffer Sharing and Synchronization", the amdgpu chapter (curriculum item 86)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F4-42 (Linux UAPI headers as installed in the build container by the package linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: <linux/kfd_ioctl.h> (ioctls, kfd_ioctl_create_queue_args, kfd_ioctl_acquire_vm_args, allocation flags, interface version 1.14), <drm/amdgpu_drm.h> (DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_*, drm_amdgpu_cs_chunk_ib, AMDGPU_HW_IP_*), <drm/drm.h> and <drm/drm_mode.h> (KMS ioctls, page-flip flags and the comments quoted in Layer 3)) — opened in this build

simple: the part of a graphics driver that controls what the screen shows.
analogy: the projector operator in the hall.
precise: the DRM interface and driver code that program the display engine: framebuffers, planes, CRTCs (scanout timing generators), encoders and connectors, mode changes and page flips, optionally as one atomic commit.
source: D1 of F4-42 (Linux kernel community, Linux kernel documentation, "GPU Driver Developer's Guide" (Documentation/gpu/): "DRM Internals", "DRM Memory Management", "Kernel Mode Setting (KMS)", "GPU Scheduler", "Buffer Sharing and Synchronization", the amdgpu chapter (curriculum item 86)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F4-42 (Linux UAPI headers as installed in the build container by the package linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: <linux/kfd_ioctl.h> (ioctls, kfd_ioctl_create_queue_args, kfd_ioctl_acquire_vm_args, allocation flags, interface version 1.14), <drm/amdgpu_drm.h> (DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_*, drm_amdgpu_cs_chunk_ib, AMDGPU_HW_IP_*), <drm/drm.h> and <drm/drm_mode.h> (KMS ioctls, page-flip flags and the comments quoted in Layer 3)) — opened in this build

simple: a small processor inside the GPU that reads the work lists and starts the work.
analogy: the stage manager who takes running orders from the board.
precise: a microcontroller block of the GPU, running vendor firmware, that fetches command packets (PM4 packets on AMD's graphics and compute rings; AQL packets from user-mode queues) and programs the GPU's engines to execute them.
source: D2 of F4-42 (Linux kernel source, drivers/gpu/drm/amd/ (amdgpu and amdkfd) (curriculum item 86; tier 4: statements are about what that code does)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D10 of F4-42 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 15.1 "What a GPU kernel driver does" and milestone G1 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build

simple: a list of jobs in memory that a program fills directly, without asking the kernel each time.
analogy: the order board at the stage door, which teachers may pin orders to themselves once they have a pass.
precise: a ring buffer of fixed-size packets in memory mapped both into the process and into the GPU's address space, with a write index, a read index and a doorbell; the kernel driver creates it (on AMD, AMDKFD_IOC_CREATE_QUEUE) and the hardware consumes it.
source: D6 of F4-42 (Linux UAPI headers as installed in the build container by the package linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: <linux/kfd_ioctl.h> (ioctls, kfd_ioctl_create_queue_args, kfd_ioctl_acquire_vm_args, allocation flags, interface version 1.14), <drm/amdgpu_drm.h> (DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_*, drm_amdgpu_cs_chunk_ib, AMDGPU_HW_IP_*), <drm/drm.h> and <drm/drm_mode.h> (KMS ioctls, page-flip flags and the comments quoted in Layer 3)) — opened in this build; D7 of F4-42 (ROCm header <hsa/hsa.h> as installed by the package libhsa-runtime-dev 5.7.1-2build1: hsa_kernel_dispatch_packet_t, hsa_packet_type_t (including the comment on HSA_PACKET_TYPE_INVALID), hsa_packet_header_t and widths, hsa_queue_t (doorbell signal comment)) — opened in this build

simple: one fixed-size job description for the GPU.
analogy: one running order on the board, written on a standard form.
precise: a 64-byte packet of the HSA Architected Queuing Language; the kernel dispatch packet holds a header (packet type, barrier bit, fence scopes), the work-group and grid sizes in work-items, segment sizes, the kernel object, the kernel-argument address and a completion signal.
source: D7 of F4-42 (ROCm header <hsa/hsa.h> as installed by the package libhsa-runtime-dev 5.7.1-2build1: hsa_kernel_dispatch_packet_t, hsa_packet_type_t (including the comment on HSA_PACKET_TYPE_INVALID), hsa_packet_header_t and widths, hsa_queue_t (doorbell signal comment)) — opened in this build; R2 of F4-42 (R2 — lab run of Listing 2: aql_queue.out, aql_queue.log (g++ 13.3.0, hsa.h from libhsa-runtime-dev 5.7.1).)

simple: a marker that says "the GPU has finished up to here".
analogy: the stage manager's "done" stamp on a running order.
precise: a synchronisation object signalled when a submitted job completes; Linux represents it as a dma-fence, which other drivers and user space can wait on; a fence that never signals is how a hang is detected (with a timeout).
source: D1 of F4-42 (Linux kernel community, Linux kernel documentation, "GPU Driver Developer's Guide" (Documentation/gpu/): "DRM Internals", "DRM Memory Management", "Kernel Mode Setting (KMS)", "GPU Scheduler", "Buffer Sharing and Synchronization", the amdgpu chapter (curriculum item 86)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a piece of memory the GPU driver manages for a program.
analogy: a numbered storage crate in the theatre's store room.
precise: a driver-managed allocation (GEM object) that may live in VRAM or in system memory, can be mapped into a process and into a GPU address space, and can be moved (evicted) by the driver's memory manager.
source: D1 of F4-42 (Linux kernel community, Linux kernel documentation, "GPU Driver Developer's Guide" (Documentation/gpu/): "DRM Internals", "DRM Memory Management", "Kernel Mode Setting (KMS)", "GPU Scheduler", "Buffer Sharing and Synchronization", the amdgpu chapter (curriculum item 86)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F4-42 (Linux UAPI headers as installed in the build container by the package linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: <linux/kfd_ioctl.h> (ioctls, kfd_ioctl_create_queue_args, kfd_ioctl_acquire_vm_args, allocation flags, interface version 1.14), <drm/amdgpu_drm.h> (DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_*, drm_amdgpu_cs_chunk_ib, AMDGPU_HW_IP_*), <drm/drm.h> and <drm/drm_mode.h> (KMS ioctls, page-flip flags and the comments quoted in Layer 3)) — opened in this build

simple: the part of AMD's Linux driver that serves ROCm compute programs.
analogy: a second door to the same interpreter, reserved for one kind of visitor.
precise: the Linux kernel driver behind /dev/kfd, part of the amdgpu module, that gives the ROCm runtime GPU memory, user-mode compute queues, events and debugging support.
source: D2 of F4-42 (Linux kernel source, drivers/gpu/drm/amd/ (amdgpu and amdkfd) (curriculum item 86; tier 4: statements are about what that code does)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F4-42 (Linux UAPI headers as installed in the build container by the package linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: <linux/kfd_ioctl.h> (ioctls, kfd_ioctl_create_queue_args, kfd_ioctl_acquire_vm_args, allocation flags, interface version 1.14), <drm/amdgpu_drm.h> (DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_*, drm_amdgpu_cs_chunk_ib, AMDGPU_HW_IP_*), <drm/drm.h> and <drm/drm_mode.h> (KMS ioctls, page-flip flags and the comments quoted in Layer 3)) — opened in this build; R3 of F4-42 (R3 — run.sh step strace: strace.out, strace.log (HIP 5.7.31921, strace 6.8; no GPU).)

simple: a pretend graphics card that virtual machines use, described in an open standard.
analogy: the company's projector, which teachers reach only through orders on the board.
precise: the virtio device type 16; its 2D command set creates host-side resources, attaches guest memory as backing, copies rectangles into resources and assigns resources to scan-outs; optional features add EDID, 3D (virgl) and blob resources.
source: D1 of F4-43 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO) Version 1.2" (or later), section "GPU Device" (curriculum Track G, G2 sources; guide registry)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F4-43 (Linux UAPI header <linux/virtio_gpu.h> and <linux/virtio_ids.h> (VIRTIO_ID_GPU 16), as installed in the build container by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146) — opened in this build

simple: an image the device keeps on its side.
analogy: a numbered slide in the company's slide store.
precise: a device-side object with an id chosen by the driver, a format and a size, created with RESOURCE_CREATE_2D; it is the device's copy of the pixels, separate from the guest's backing memory.
source: D1 of F4-43 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO) Version 1.2" (or later), section "GPU Device" (curriculum Track G, G2 sources; guide registry)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F4-43 (Linux UAPI header <linux/virtio_gpu.h> and <linux/virtio_ids.h> (VIRTIO_ID_GPU 16), as installed in the build container by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146) — opened in this build

simple: the guest's own memory where the driver draws the pixels.
analogy: the teacher's drawing in her classroom.
precise: a list of guest-physical memory ranges attached to a resource with RESOURCE_ATTACH_BACKING; TRANSFER_TO_HOST_2D copies a rectangle from it into the resource.
source: D1 of F4-43 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO) Version 1.2" (or later), section "GPU Device" (curriculum Track G, G2 sources; guide registry)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F4-43 (Linux UAPI header <linux/virtio_gpu.h> and <linux/virtio_ids.h> (VIRTIO_ID_GPU 16), as installed in the build container by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146) — opened in this build

simple: one output of a graphics card, like one monitor connector.
analogy: the projector.
precise: a display output of the device (virtio-gpu reports up to 16); SET_SCANOUT selects which resource, and which rectangle of it, the output shows. In real hardware the term also means the act of reading a framebuffer out to the display, line by line (F4-46).
source: D2 of F4-43 (Linux UAPI header <linux/virtio_gpu.h> and <linux/virtio_ids.h> (VIRTIO_ID_GPU 16), as installed in the build container by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146) — opened in this build

simple: the part of the screen that changed.
analogy: the bit of the drawing the teacher re-did, so only that part is copied onto the slide.
precise: a rectangle (or set of rectangles) bounding all pixels that differ between two frames; a driver or compositor sends and shows only that region to save copying.
source: R2 of F4-43 (R2 — run.sh step vgpu: vgpu.out, vgpu.log (QEMU 8.2.2, TCG, q35, virtio-gpu-pci,xres=640,yres=480).)

simple: a small block of data in which a monitor describes itself.
analogy: the projector's label: maker, model, and the picture sizes it can show.
precise: Extended Display Identification Data, a 128-byte base block (plus 128-byte extension blocks) with a fixed header, manufacturer and product ids, supported timings and detailed timing descriptors; read over DDC on real hardware and with GET_EDID on virtio-gpu. F4-46 parses it.
source: D2 of F4-43 (Linux UAPI header <linux/virtio_gpu.h> and <linux/virtio_ids.h> (VIRTIO_ID_GPU 16), as installed in the build container by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146) — opened in this build; D4 of F4-43 (VESA, "Enhanced Extended Display Identification Data Standard (E-EDID)", Release A, Revision 2 (curriculum G5 sources)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a picture file of what a virtual monitor shows right now.
analogy: a photograph of the hall's screen taken from the back row.
precise: QEMU's monitor command screendump, which writes the current contents of the guest display, here as a binary PPM file; it is the evidence for G2's acceptance test.
source: D3 of F4-43 (QEMU 8.2.2 as installed in the build container: the trace-event list trace-events-all (the virtio_gpu_* events) and the monitor commands screendump and sendkey as used in the runs. Trace-event list opened in this build; QEMU's documentation and source were not opened) — opened in this build; R3 of F4-43 (R3 — run.sh step screens: screens.out, screens.log.)

simple: a small memory chip on a card that holds code and data for the computer's firmware.
analogy: the instruction booklet taped to the first crate.
precise: a read-only image on a PCI device, mapped into memory through the ROM BAR, made of one or more images, each starting with the signature 0x55 0xAA and containing a PCI data structure that names the device and the code type (x86 legacy, UEFI, …).
source: D1 of F4-44 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Firmware Specification", chapter "PCI Expansion ROMs" (curriculum reading-list item 37)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F4-44 (Linux UAPI header <linux/pci_regs.h> as installed by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: PCI_ROM_ADDRESS (0x30), PCI_ROM_ADDRESS_ENABLE (0x01), PCI_ROM_ADDRESS_MASK, the BAR bits and the capability IDs used by DR301's pci.h) — opened in this build

simple: the setting that decides where the card's ROM appears in memory, and whether it appears at all.
analogy: the reading lamp on the crate.
precise: the configuration register at offset 0x30 of a type 0 header (PCI_ROM_ADDRESS); bits 31–11 hold the address, bit 0 (PCI_ROM_ADDRESS_ENABLE) enables decoding; the device answers reads in the ROM window only while the bit and memory decoding in the command register are both set.
source: D2 of F4-44 (Linux UAPI header <linux/pci_regs.h> as installed by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: PCI_ROM_ADDRESS (0x30), PCI_ROM_ADDRESS_ENABLE (0x01), PCI_ROM_ADDRESS_MASK, the BAR bits and the capability IDs used by DR301's pci.h) — opened in this build; R2 of F4-44 (R2 — run.sh step probe: probe.out, probe.log (QEMU 8.2.2, TCG, q35).)

simple: a label inside the ROM that says which card it is for.
analogy: the booklet's title page: company name, model, edition.
precise: a structure inside an expansion-ROM image, found through the 16-bit pointer at offset 0x18, starting with the ASCII signature "PCIR" and holding the vendor and device IDs, class code, image length in 512-byte units, code type and the last-image flag.
source: D1 of F4-44 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Firmware Specification", chapter "PCI Expansion ROMs" (curriculum reading-list item 37)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F4-44 (R1 — lab run of romcheck.cpp: romcheck.out, romcheck.log (SeaBIOS 1.16.3-2 images).)

simple: the graphics card's own start-up program and settings table.
analogy: the booklet, which on some companies' crates also lists every setting of the rig.
precise: the expansion ROM of a display device; its legacy x86 image sets up a text or VESA mode at boot; on AMD GPUs it also holds the ATOM BIOS command and data tables that the amdgpu driver reads.
source: D3 of F4-44 (Linux kernel source, drivers/gpu/drm/amd/: include/atombios.h, include/atomfirmware.h, amdgpu/atom.c, amdgpu/amdgpu_atombios.c, amdgpu/amdgpu_bios.c (curriculum G3 "Read"; item 86)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D5 of F4-44 (Linux kernel documentation, amdgpu chapter ("drm/amdgpu AMDgpu driver"), including its debugfs and VBIOS information) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: AMD's format for the tables and little scripts inside its graphics BIOS.
analogy: the booklet's appendix of settings, written in the company's own shorthand.
precise: AMD's VBIOS table format: a ROM header points to a master command table and a master data table, each a list of offsets to individual tables (clock information, display objects, power tables, …); the amdgpu driver parses the data tables and interprets the command tables.
source: D3 of F4-44 (Linux kernel source, drivers/gpu/drm/amd/: include/atombios.h, include/atomfirmware.h, amdgpu/atom.c, amdgpu/amdgpu_atombios.c, amdgpu/amdgpu_bios.c (curriculum G3 "Read"; item 86)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a copy of the graphics card's start-up program that the PC firmware puts in ordinary memory.
analogy: the caretaker's photocopy of the booklet, possibly with notes in the margin.
precise: the legacy VGA option ROM image that the system BIOS copies to memory at 0xC0000 and runs; it can differ from the device's ROM because the code may modify its own copy during initialisation.
source: D4 of F4-44 (SeaBIOS project, documentation and source of its VGA BIOS (the images in /usr/share/seabios/, package seabios 1.16.3-2, were parsed in this build; the documentation and source were not opened)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F4-44 (R2 — run.sh step probe: probe.out, probe.log (QEMU 8.2.2, TCG, q35).)

simple: the vendor's own book about how to program its chip.
analogy: the full printed scripts a company leaves in the library.
precise: Intel's Graphics Programmer's Reference Manuals, published per generation, in volumes covering the display engine, render and media engines, memory interface and command formats; coverage differs by generation (curriculum 16.1).
source: D2 of F4-45 (Intel, "Intel Graphics Programmer's Reference Manuals (PRMs)", per generation (reading-list item 164)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D1 of F4-45 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 16 "Open GPU documentation beyond AMD and NVIDIA": 16.1 (table), 16.2, 16.3 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build

simple: the big manual for a whole chip, with every block's registers.
analogy: the school building's complete plans, including the hall's projector room.
precise: a SoC vendor's document describing each on-chip block and its registers; for display controllers it is often the only documentation needed (NXP and TI publish them fully, according to curriculum 16.1).
source: D1 of F4-45 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 16 "Open GPU documentation beyond AMD and NVIDIA": 16.1 (table), 16.2, 16.3 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build

simple: working out how a chip is programmed by watching what its official driver does.
analogy: the drama club's notes from years of watching rehearsals.
precise: lawful observation of a vendor driver's interaction with the hardware (traced memory-mapped I/O, captured command streams, hypervisor-based observation as in Asahi Linux's m1n1), followed by experiments that confirm each hypothesis; the method of DR401 at scale.
source: D1 of F4-45 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 16 "Open GPU documentation beyond AMD and NVIDIA": 16.1 (table), 16.2, 16.3 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build; D5 of F4-45 (Asahi Linux project, documentation wiki and m1n1 source (item 156); envytools and NVIDIA's open-gpu-doc repository (item 167)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much of the GPU only works after a vendor's secret program is loaded into it.
analogy: stage managers who work only from sealed, signed scripts.
precise: the set of signed firmware binaries a driver must load before an engine works (command processors, power management, security, a command-stream front end); "everything" means no engine runs without it, which puts the hardware interface behind an interface defined by the vendor's firmware.
source: D1 of F4-45 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 16 "Open GPU documentation beyond AMD and NVIDIA": 16.1 (table), 16.2, 16.3 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build; R1 of F4-45 (R1 — lab run of uapi_survey.cpp: uapi_survey.out, uapi_survey.log (headers from linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146).)

simple: the part of a chip that sends a picture to the screen.
analogy: the projector and its operator, separate from the actors.
precise: the hardware block that reads framebuffers from memory, composes planes and generates the timing for one or more outputs (called a pipe, CRTC, VOP, DSS or HVS depending on the vendor); it needs no shader compiler and on SoCs usually no firmware.
source: D1 of F4-45 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 16 "Open GPU documentation beyond AMD and NVIDIA": 16.1 (table), 16.2, 16.3 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build

simple: the open-source collection of user-space graphics drivers on Linux.
analogy: the shared workshop where every company's stage crew builds sets.
precise: the project that contains the OpenGL and Vulkan drivers for most open GPU kernel drivers, with a shared compiler infrastructure (NIR) and the Gallium driver framework; for a hobby kernel it is the realistic source of a shader compiler.
source: D3 of F4-45 (Linux kernel source drivers/gpu/drm/ (panfrost, lima, msm, vc4, v3d, imagination, etnaviv, i915, xe, nouveau) and the Mesa source tree (reading-list items 40, 87, 166)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D1 of F4-45 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 16 "Open GPU documentation beyond AMD and NVIDIA": 16.1 (table), 16.2, 16.3 (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build

simple: the short pause after the screen has been drawn to the bottom and before it starts again at the top.
analogy: the dark moment between two showings of a slide.
precise: the lines of a video frame after the last active line (in the 640 × 480 mode of R1, lines 480–495 of 496) during which no visible pixels are scanned out; display engines latch double-buffered registers such as the surface address at its start.
source: D2 of F4-46 (Linux UAPI header <drm/drm_mode.h> as installed by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: struct drm_mode_modeinfo, struct drm_mode_crtc_page_flip, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_EVENT, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_ASYNC and the comments quoted) — opened in this build; R1 of F4-46 (R1 — run.sh step edid_test: edid_test.out, edid_test.log.)

simple: telling the display to show a different picture buffer.
analogy: changing slides.
precise: changing a plane's scanout (surface) address to another framebuffer; a synchronised flip takes effect at the next vertical blank and its completion is reported by an event; Linux's DRM_IOCTL_MODE_PAGE_FLIP schedules one.
source: D2 of F4-46 (Linux UAPI header <drm/drm_mode.h> as installed by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: struct drm_mode_modeinfo, struct drm_mode_crtc_page_flip, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_EVENT, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_ASYNC and the comments quoted) — opened in this build

simple: a visible line where the top of the screen shows one picture and the bottom another.
analogy: swapping the slide while it is being projected.
precise: the artefact of changing the scanout address while active lines are being scanned out, so that one refresh shows parts of two buffers; the DRM header warns that DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_ASYNC "may cause tearing on the screen".
source: D2 of F4-46 (Linux UAPI header <drm/drm_mode.h> as installed by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: struct drm_mode_modeinfo, struct drm_mode_crtc_page_flip, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_EVENT, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_ASYNC and the comments quoted) — opened in this build; R2 of F4-46 (R2 — lab run of flipsim.cpp: flipsim.out, flipsim.log (a model, not a measurement).)

simple: the screen size together with how fast the pixels are sent.
analogy: the projector's settings: slide size, painting speed, length of the dark moment.
precise: a pixel clock and horizontal and vertical timings (active, sync start, sync end, total) with sync polarities; struct drm_mode_modeinfo holds exactly these fields.
source: D2 of F4-46 (Linux UAPI header <drm/drm_mode.h> as installed by linux-libc-dev 6.8.0-146.146: struct drm_mode_modeinfo, struct drm_mode_crtc_page_flip, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_EVENT, DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_ASYNC and the comments quoted) — opened in this build; R1 of F4-46 (R1 — run.sh step edid_test: edid_test.out, edid_test.log.)

simple: an 18-byte entry in the EDID that describes one mode exactly.
analogy: one line of the projector's label giving all settings for one slide size.
precise: an EDID descriptor with the pixel clock in units of 10 kHz and 12-bit (horizontal) and 10/6-bit (vertical) active, blanking, sync offset and width fields split across bytes; the first descriptor is the preferred timing.
source: D3 of F4-46 (VESA, "Enhanced Extended Display Identification Data Standard (E-EDID)", Release A, Revision 2) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F4-46 (R1 — run.sh step edid_test: edid_test.out, edid_test.log.)

simple: the small controller in an Intel GPU that talks to the monitor to read its EDID.
analogy: the intercom to the projector room.
precise: Intel's I²C controller in the display engine, used for DDC to read EDID from a connected monitor (named in curriculum G5's reading list).

simple: a careful written check of whether a project can be done, before doing it.
analogy: the drama club's report on the scenery lift.
precise: in Track G, a document that "lists every firmware blob, register block and documentation gap needed" (G4) for one engine and one job, with risks, a stop criterion and a verification method; an acceptable outcome on its own for G4 and G6.
source: D4 of F4-47 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone G4 (section 15), section 16.1, 16.3 and milestone G6 (section 16.4) (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build

simple: a rule, written in advance, for when to stop.
analogy: "if we cannot find out how the lift's brake works, we do not touch the lift".
precise: a condition in a study (for example, "the power-up sequence cannot be documented from the guide or the open driver") that ends the project after the study, decided before effort or hope can bias it.

simple: working out which pixels a shape covers.
analogy: deciding which floor tiles of the stage a painted triangle touches.
precise: converting a primitive (here a triangle in screen coordinates) into the set of pixel samples it covers, usually by testing each pixel centre against the triangle's three edge functions.
source: R1 of F4-47 (R1 — lab run of ref_triangle.cpp: ref_triangle.out, ref_triangle.log.)

simple: a calculation that says on which side of a line a point is.
analogy: standing on a chalk line and asking "am I to its left or right?".
precise: for an edge from a to b and a point p, (b.x − a.x)(p.y − a.y) − (b.y − a.y)(p.x − a.x); its sign tells the side, zero means on the line; for a consistently wound triangle, a point is inside when all three are non-negative (subject to the fill rule).
source: R1 of F4-47 (R1 — lab run of ref_triangle.cpp: ref_triangle.out, ref_triangle.log.)

simple: the tie-break for pixels exactly on the edge of a shape.
analogy: a tile on the line between two painted triangles belongs to exactly one of them, by an agreed rule.
precise: a convention that includes a pixel whose centre lies exactly on an edge only if that edge is a "top" or "left" edge, so that triangles sharing an edge cover each pixel exactly once; which rule a given GPU applies is defined by its documentation.
source: R1 of F4-47 (R1 — lab run of ref_triangle.cpp: ref_triangle.out, ref_triangle.log.); D1 of F4-47 (Broadcom, "VideoCore IV 3D Architecture Reference Guide" (reading-list item 165)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of instructions the Raspberry Pi's 3D core reads to draw.
analogy: the running order for one show.
precise: a sequence of packets in memory that the VideoCore IV 3D core's binner and renderer execute (state, primitives, tile operations), named in curriculum G6 and defined in Broadcom's architecture guide.
source: D1 of F4-47 (Broadcom, "VideoCore IV 3D Architecture Reference Guide" (reading-list item 165)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D4 of F4-47 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone G4 (section 15), section 16.1, 16.3 and milestone G6 (section 16.4) (a map to sources, AH-4; opened in this build)) — opened in this build
